# Color

Each layer has its surface color. A surface tone separates before any shadow; Sunken marks a different surface, never a recess. In dark mode only floating and blocking surfaces step lighter.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/ElevationColor.mdx`

## States and adaptive fills

| Token | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `-hovered · -pressed` | Every surface has both. A clickable surface changes tone on hover and press; a clickable Sunken card lifts to Raised on hover instead. Never both at once. |
| `--ds-background-neutral` | Translucent: darkens in light, lightens in dark. For a fill that must adapt to whatever surface it sits on (a button, a tag). Not a container. |

## Colored surfaces

A surface token may be swapped for a solid background token when the color means something: brand, status or selection.

### Swap the surface; never stack it

## Dark mode

Shadows read weakly on dark surfaces, so floating and blocking surfaces step lighter. Which ones step lighter is rule 9 under Usage; here is how.

Raised is the exception: in dark it keeps the page tone (`--ds-surface-raised` equals `--ds-surface`), so a Raised card separates by its shadow alone and never steps lighter.
